quote.text: A cynic is a man who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing.
quote.author: Oscar Wilde, Lady Windermere's Fan (1892)

stories.headline: Iran Draws the Corridor — and a Toll Booth
stories.dek: Tehran says it has agreed the coordinates of a new Hormuz shipping route with Oman. Read past the map to the clause the shipowners are already fighting: a sixty-day grace period, and then a fee to cross a strait no state has ever been allowed to charge for.

stories.headline: The Cruise You Take Twenty-Five Times
stories.dek: Most people take a cruise once. A devoted core takes the Disney one again and again — chasing a loyalty tier that tops out at twenty-five sailings, decorating stateroom doors, and exchanging gifts with strangers at sea. And this year, the whole global hobby docked in Singapore.

stories.headline: Life in Four Cuts
stories.dek: In the most camera-saturated country on earth, young Koreans queue to pay ₩4,000 for a strip of four printed photographs. It has become a US$400-million industry — and, in the same breath, a franchise bubble bursting in plain sight. The West hasn't noticed yet.

stories.headline: A Parade Under a Roof, a Speech in a Fortnight
stories.dek: National Day returns to the National Stadium on Sunday with the country's first indoor drone show and a "Go Beyond" theme. The number that will actually shape a household lands two Sundays later, when the Prime Minister rises for the National Day Rally.

stories.headline: The Showflats Sell Out; the Land Bank Goes Quiet
stories.dek: Singapore's new-launch condos are clearing at 88 to 94% in a year with roughly a third fewer projects than the last. In the same market, a state land tender drew a single bid. Buyers are paying up and developers are holding back — the premium is moving to the finished flat.

stories.headline: The Best Open Model on Earth Is Free — and Chinese
stories.dek: Moonshot's Kimi K3 shipped its full weights in late July at 2.8 trillion parameters, the largest open-weight model ever released, and independent scoring places it above Claude Opus 4.8. The premium the frontier labs charge for is the thing a Chinese lab just gave away.

stories.headline: The Camera That Skips the Bag of Lenses
stories.dek: Nine years after the last one, Sony has revived its bridge camera as the RX10 V — a single body that reaches from 24 to 600mm, ships this month, and costs about US$2,300. The premium buys reach and never changing a lens. The fine print is the sensor at its heart, which is the same one from 2017.

stories.headline: A Ryokan That Watches the Floating Torii
stories.dek: Hoshino's next KAI onsen house opens this summer across the water from Miyajima's great vermilion gate — fifty-four rooms, every one facing the sea, and a bath reviving a method the region had nearly forgotten.

stories.headline: A Billion in Six Days, and Then the Real Test
stories.dek: Spider-Man crossed a billion dollars faster than almost any film ever made — a premium the marketing machine pre-sold before a single review landed. The number that will actually measure it is next weekend's drop. Meanwhile the album calendar fills: three releases in a fortnight, and the reviews, unlike the receipts, aren't in.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Real Lever
stories.headline: It Was Never the Screen. It Was the Sleep.
stories.dek: A new analysis of the largest child-brain study in the world finds that among the things a parent can actually change, sleep — not screen time — is the strongest thread between how a ten-to-thirteen-year-old feels and how she does at school and with friends. The highest-yield rule in the house is a bedtime, not an app.

stories.headline: The Relief Trade Runs Out of Road
stories.dek: Records on Tuesday, a reversal by Thursday. Yields rose, the dollar firmed and oil bounced, and the Dow's record streak snapped — all before the one number that could settle it lands tonight. Gold, at a record, is charging the highest premium of all.

stories.headline: The Weighted Walk Is Having a Moment — With Numbers
stories.dek: Rucking — walking with a loaded pack — is 2026's defining longevity method, and for once the hype comes with a ratio behind it: a fraction of running's injury rate, several times a walk's training stimulus, and a strength-and-bone dose folded into a cardio session. The catch is in how fast you load the bar.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking
stories.dek: A crowded autumn to plan around: Singapore's first F1 Sprint weekend with a Padang full of pop beside it, and a Tokyo sumo basho whose good seats vanish the morning they go on sale — which is tomorrow.
